card.title: We Keep Switching Places
card.instruction: Return to a familiar relationship pattern, then reverse who performs each role whenever the scene reaches similar pressure.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The tap's leaking again. Give me the spanner before you start pricing lifeboats.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've found the valve. You look terrified.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you fix it. I'll keep the towels ready for when the kitchen goes under.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The valve's stuck. What if I snap it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the spanner. You take the towels; you've reached the sinking-kitchen stage.

mechanism: A and B swap fixer and catastrophizer roles each time the leak threatens the person currently in control.
confusable: Unlike general panic, similar pressure must trigger recognizable reversals of a familiar two-person pattern.
comparison: S225-a swaps spanner and towels with each threatened failure; S225-b swaps reassurance roles across equipment failures.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
